_comment: Protagonist observations and future NPC dialogue. Each entry: lines [{speaker, text, time}] and optional choices [{text, next}] for future branching.

lines.text: Ugh. That was supposed to be a twenty-minute nap.
Stomach's growling. Let's see what's in the kitchen.
Great. Nothing to eat.
One dented can and a bottle of water. Grocery run it is.
Still empty. Staring at it won't help.
Keys. Right where I left them, for once.
Locked. My keys are still inside.
Better check what I actually need before I drive anywhere.
Still light out. Supermarket's open till nine.
Come on, start... There we go.
Main Street. Supermarket's on the right, across from the game shop.
Might swing by the game shop after. Something scary for tonight.
Not while it's moving.
No room to open the door here.
Made it. Groceries, then the game shop. Or the other way round.
Already evening. I slept right through the afternoon.
Friday. Finally.
Nothing worth watching at this hour.
Beat everything on here twice. I need something new to play.
Empty box. Who puts an empty box back?
Me. I do.
Later.
Talk radio and the weather. Nothing new.
Getting late. Better move.

_comment_phase2: Entries marked draft:true are Phase 2 working lines (Eddie, the unnamed cashier). The bible names no cashier, so 'Cashier' is a placeholder speaker. Replace when the script is written.

lines.text: Soup, water, something to snack on. In and out.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Still shopping? Soup, water and snacks are in aisles one, two and four, hon.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: That's everything? Bag's on the house.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Drive safe tonight.
Groceries, done.
Smells like old carpet and new plastic. Love it.
This one. Looks properly scary.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Hey! Back again. The new stuff's on the front rack.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Oh, good pick. Don't play that one with the lights off.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Seriously. Enjoy your Friday.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Let me know how far you get.
That's everything. Home, food, game.

_comment_phase3: p3_* entries: Phase 3 (Act I opening, WORKING DRAFT). All draft. Noah's age is TBD, so Marcus only says 'my son'.

lines.text: The lights... what's going on out there?
That's not normal fog.
Inside. Get inside. NOW.
Come on, start. Start!
Dead. Even the radio's just static.
Still dead.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Hey! HEY! Over here - get inside, now!

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Don't just stand there!

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Tell me you saw that. Please tell me you saw that.
I saw it.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: My son is out there. Noah. Have you seen him?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Nobody's seen anything, man. Ten minutes ago it was a normal Friday.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: I'm not leaving him out there.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Then we regroup first. The supermarket - food, water, a back room.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Fine. We go now, before it gets any thicker.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Go! We'll cut through the back and meet you there. Stay away from those... things.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Noah knows this street. If he's smart, he's hiding somewhere.
Agh! Get away from me!
Where is everyone? The cashier was right here.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: You made it. The power's out - the doors are stuck open!

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Shut them. Now!
Okay. Okay. We're inside.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: For now.
I've already got one.
Ugh... I made it back in. Barely.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Okay. Nobody panic. Well - panic quietly.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: It's pitch black in here.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: The breaker's in the back room, by the loading door. Customer service keeps a flashlight under the desk.
Customer service. Right.
Flashlight. And a pack of batteries.
F turns it on. R swaps the batteries.
Staff only. Tonight that's me.
Can't see a thing back here.
Come on...
There. Emergency lights, at least.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: We've got light! Sort of!
It's on. That's all it's got.
The loading door isn't all the way down. The mist is getting in under it.
Down. Now something heavy in front of it.
The back door's open. Who left it open?
Closed. It won't hold if something pushes, though.
Close the door first.
Let's see it get through that.
That's every way in. Back to the others.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Are the doors shut? All of them?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Check the back first. I'm not sleeping until I know nothing can walk in.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Lights are on. Good. Then I'm going back out.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Out where? You saw what's out there.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: My son is out there. Every minute I wait is a minute he's alone.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: And out there you can't see your own hand. You'd be walking around blind.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Then what? We sit here eating chips while he's-

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Hey. Hey. Ask them. You were out there too.

choices.text: "We can't just leave Noah out there."

lines.text: We should wait until morning. We can't help him if we get lost out there too.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: ...First light. Not a minute later.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: First light. I'll go with you.
We can't just leave Noah out there.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Nobody's leaving him. But nobody's walking into that blind, either.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Then we go the moment it thins. I mean it.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Fine. First light. Together.
...Did you hear that?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Don't. Move.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Something hit the back door.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: ...It's gone. I think it's gone.
What was that?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Not a dog. Too big for a dog.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Okay. New rule: nobody goes near the glass.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Get some sleep. There's room in the office - I found blankets in aisle six. I'll take first watch.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Wake me in two hours.
Not yet. Not while that thing's out there.
Morning. I think.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Morning. Or whatever we're calling it.
Did you sleep?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Not really. Every time the building made a noise, I thought something was coming through the doors.
We need more supplies.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Yeah. I checked what we have left. It's not great.
There's a neighborhood close by.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: You're suggesting we go outside again.
We don't have much choice.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Right. Great. Love having choices.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: I've been looking at the streets around here.
Find anything?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Not yet. But Noah knew this part of town. He could've gone somewhere familiar.
We're going to look for supplies first.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Just... if you see anything. Anything that might belong to him.
I'll keep an eye out.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Okay. Quick trip. In and out.
That's the plan.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Good. Because I've got absolutely no interest in becoming a missing-person poster.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: It's weird seeing everything like this.
Quiet?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Yeah. Yesterday people were arguing over parking spaces. Now look at it.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Someone left in a hurry.
Looks that way.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: I hope they made it somewhere safe.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Okay. That's something.
We should keep looking.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Just don't get too comfortable.

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: ...temperatures expected to remain mild through the evening...

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: ...drivers are advised to use caution in areas of reduced visibility...

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [STATIC]

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: ...and now, back to your regularly scheduled programming...

lines.speaker: Radio
lines.text: [STATIC]

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Did you hear that?
Yeah.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: That sounded normal.
Too normal.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Think someone's still broadcasting?
I don't know.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Well, that's reassuring.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: Who's there?
We're looking for supplies. We're not here to hurt you.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: Are you alone?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: There's two of us.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: Are those things still outside?
Yes.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: I can't stay here forever.

choices.text: "We have a place nearby. It's safer than staying here alone."
"There's a supermarket nearby. We've secured the entrances."

lines.text: We have a place nearby. It's safer than staying here alone.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: You're sure?
It's the best we've got.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: Okay. I'll follow you.
There's a supermarket nearby. We've secured the entrances.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: I'll try to get there.
We have to go.

lines.speaker: Survivor
lines.text: Wait—

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: I think that's enough excitement for one day.
We got what we needed.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Mostly.
Mostly?

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: I was hoping we'd also find a working television and a way out of town.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: You're back.
We found some supplies.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Anything else?
A radio was still broadcasting.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Someone's out there, then.

lines.speaker: Eddie
lines.text: Maybe. It didn't sound like anyone knew what was happening.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Did you see anything about Noah?
Not yet.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Then we keep looking.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: You brought someone back.
They needed somewhere safe.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Then we'll make room.
